newsitem.title: USA: Plains completes short radius well.
newsitem.headline: Plains completes short radius well.

text.p: Plains Resources Inc said its first short radius horizontal well has been drilled and completed in the West Felda Field in Hendry County, Florida.
The company said the Turner Corp No. 30-5 was drilled to a vertical depth 11,455 feet and achieved a lateral extension of approximately 790 feet within the Sunniland formation.

The company said the well has averaged in excess of 1,000 barrels of oil per day since being placed on electrical submersible pump. It is currently producing some 3,600 barrels per day of total fluid, resulting in a total oil cut of about 30 perecnt.
While the oil cut is expected to fluctuate as the well stabilizes and will decrease over time as the well depletes, previous company estimates targeted an initial oil cut of about 15 percent.
Plains holds a 100 percent working interest and an 84 percent net revenue interest in this well and said it plans up to four additional short radius horizontal wells in South Florida in 1997.

The company also said its initial exploratory well on the Four Isle Dome 3-D project in Terrebonne Parish, La., was a dry hole. The LL&E State Unit 17 No. 1 well was drilled to a depth of 13,650 feet, encountering the primary objective sands. Electric logs indicate these sands are not productive.

Plains said its cost bearing interest in the LL&E State Unit 17 No. 1 is about 30 percent. A second well is scheduled to start drilling on the north flank of the salt dome structure in late December or early January.
